accounting_policy.policy_risk_note: FY2024 marks the second consecutive useful-life extension for Meta's server fleet within three years (2022: 4→5 years; 2024: 5→5.5 years). The 2024 extension is modest (+0.5 years) but follows the same pattern: each extension reduces depreciation expense prospectively, leaving prior-year profits unadjusted. The cumulative effect is a server fleet now depreciated over 5.5 years vs. an AI hardware cycle of 1-2 years - a 2.75-5.5x mismatch. Management justification (improved maintenance, longer actual usage) is identical to 2022. The $2.9B expected 2025 savings (~4.6% of FY2024 net income) is material.

risk_signals.source: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In January 2024, we completed an assessment of the useful lives of our servers and network assets and revised the estimated useful life of our servers and network assets to 5.5 years, effective beginning fiscal year 2024. We expect this change to reduce our full-year 2025 depreciation expense by approximately $2.9 billion.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies (HTML L4564-L4567)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: This is the SECOND useful-life extension for Meta's server fleet within three years (2022: 4→4.5→5 years; 2024: 5→5.5 years), establishing a clear pattern of optimistic life estimates. The cumulative effect extends server depreciation from 4 to 5.5 years (+37.5%) vs. an AI hardware cycle of 1-2 years. The $2.9B expected annual savings is material (~4.6% of FY2024 net income). The change is applied prospectively, meaning historical depreciation expense is NOT restated - prior-year profits remain inflated by the earlier extensions.
evidence_chain: January 2024 assessment completed: servers and network assets extended to 5.5 years (from 5 years)
Effective beginning FY2024; applied prospectively (no retrospective adjustment)
Expected to reduce full-year 2025 depreciation by ~$2.9B
This follows the 2022 extension (4→5 years) that reduced depreciation by ~$860M in 2022 and additional amounts in 2023
Cumulative effect: server depreciation now 5.5 years vs. AI hardware cycle of 1-2 years → mismatch ratio 2.75-5.5x
Pattern established: repeated extensions suggest initial estimates were systematically too short, or management is using estimate changes to manage earnings

risk_signals.text_excerpt: Depreciation expense on property and equipment was $15.29 billion, $11.02 billion, and $8.50 billion for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. Server assets depreciation expenses were $11.34 billion, $7.32 billion, and $5.29 billion for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Despite the 2022 and 2024 useful-life extensions, server depreciation still grew 114% in two years ($5.29B→$11.34B), driven by massive CAPEX ($37.3B in 2024). Total depreciation grew 80% ($8.50B→$15.29B). The $2.9B "savings" from the 2024 extension is dwarfed by the scale of new asset additions - the fleet is expanding so fast that even with longer lives, depreciation expense is exploding. This is the classic depreciation arms race: more assets + longer lives = even higher future depreciation reversal risk when the fleet eventually turns over.
evidence_chain: The 2024 extension "saves" $2.9B, but new assets added in 2024 alone generate ~$7-8B annual depreciation (straight-line, 5.5 years)
Result: depreciation expense trajectory is upward despite extensions; reversal risk accumulates in the depreciable base

risk_signals.text_excerpt: We face significant competition in almost every aspect of our business, including from companies that provide applications to users on mobile devices... We also compete with companies that develop and deliver virtual and augmented reality devices and platforms... Our industry is also characterized by rapidly evolving technology and frequent new product introductions.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Meta acknowledges rapid technology evolution in Risk Factors, directly contradicting the 5.5-year server depreciation assumption. AI training hardware (H100→B100→B200) iterates every 12-18 months. The 2024 extension to 5.5 years assumes servers remain economically useful for 66 months - 3.3-5.5x the actual hardware cycle.
evidence_chain: Risk Factor: "rapidly evolving technology and frequent new product introductions"
AI accelerator cycle: H100 (2022) → B100 (2024) → B200 (2025): ~12-18 months
Server depreciation life: 5.5 years = 66 months
Mismatch ratio: 66/12 = 5.5x to 66/18 = 3.7x
Result: depreciation expense materially understates economic consumption

dimension_scores.dimension_name: 折旧年限 vs 技术实际寿命
dimension_scores.dimension_name_en: Depreciation Life vs Technology Useful Life
dimension_scores.reasoning: META 2024将服务器年限从5年进一步延长至5.5年，是三年内第二次延长（2022: 4→5年；2024: 5→5.5年）。累积效应使服务器折旧年限从4年增至5.5年（+37.5%），而AI硬件迭代周期仍为1-2年。错配比例从2022年的2-2.5x恶化到2024年的2.75-5.5x。5.5年直线法折旧意味着年折旧率仅18.2%，而硬件经济寿命可能在12-18个月后就因新一代GPU迭代而大幅贬值。评5分（锚点与2022/2023一致，但累积错配更严重）。
2024年再次采用未来适用法（prospectively）延长年限，与2022年手法一致。三年内两次延长、两次均为未来适用法，历史利润从未被追溯调整。$2.9B的2025年"节省"完全来自会计估计变更而非经营改善。锚点：多次未来适用法延长 → 5分（与2022/2023一致）。
FY2024未计提重大长期资产减值（延续2021-2023零减值记录），但减值风险因素在积累：(1) Reality Labs连续四年巨亏（$17.7B），相关资产组合存在减值触发条件；(2) 服务器折旧年限两次延长后，资产账面价值被抬高，未来技术替代时减值压力更大；(3) 减值测试采用未折现现金流（弱兜底）。评3分（与2023年持平，风险积累但尚未触发）。
CAPEX/收入=22.7%（2024），2025年指引$60-65B将进一步推高至~30%。PP&E净值$121.3B，年折旧$15.3B但服务器折旧$11.3B。折旧假设偏差的杠杆效应极大：若5.5年高估20%（实际4.4年），年费用少计约$2.5-3B。评5分（与2023年一致，CAPEX强度持续走高）。

三重替代压力：(1) AI军备竞赛——OpenAI/Google/Amazon/xAI等竞相建设更大训练集群，Meta必须持续升级硬件以保持竞争力；(2) TPU自研vs NVIDIA GPU——Meta同时采购NVIDIA GPU和自研MTIA芯片，硬件路线不确定性增加淘汰风险；(3) 广告市场——TikTok/短视频持续侵蚀用户时长，AI推荐算法迭代加速。评5分（与2023年一致，竞争烈度未减）。

composite_score.confidence_reason: Direct verbatim evidence for the 2024 useful-life extension (Note 1, HTML L4564) with quantified $2.9B impact. Two consecutive extensions within three years establish a clear pattern. All financial data (revenue, capex, depreciation) is directly extracted from the 10-K. The only uncertainty is the precise economic life of AI training hardware (industry estimate 1-2 years, but Meta may achieve longer actual usage through maintenance).

comparative_context.same_company_trend: META 2022 (4 years) → 2023 (5 years) → 2024 (5.5 years): three-year trend of repeated useful-life extensions, each applied prospectively. Server depreciation grew from $5.3B to $11.3B (+114%) despite extensions, due to massive CAPEX growth.
comparative_context.cross_company_benchmark: Among the cloud cohort, Meta has the most aggressive useful-life extension pattern: GOOGL 2022 (4→6 years, one-time), MSFT 2022 (4→6 years, one-time), META 2022+2024 (4→5→5.5 years, two-time). Only Meta shows repeated extensions.
comparative_context.narrative_significance: Meta is the clearest case of "depreciation optimism creep" — each extension is small (+0.5-1.5 years) but the cumulative effect is large (+1.5 years over 3 years, +37.5%). The prospective application means each extension permanently inflates the depreciable base. With $60-65B CAPEX guidance for 2025, the depreciation arms race is accelerating.
